chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Mansur ibn al-Abbas from Sa'id ibn Janah who said: Abu Mash'ar narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever says 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin' four times in the morning has fulfilled the gratitude of his day, and whoever says it in the evening has fulfilled the gratitude of his night.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin four times morning and evening?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the profound spiritual efficacy of repeating the opening verse of Surah Al-Fatiha four times upon waking and at dusk, framing it as a complete discharge of daily gratitude (shukr). This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating Quranic recitation into daily rhythms to maintain constant awareness of Allah as the Lord of all worlds. By linking specific times of day with this dhikr, the hadith provides a structured method for believers to cultivate a continuous state of thankfulness throughout their waking hours.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan from Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Mansur b. al-Abbas from Sa’eed b. Janah who said it was narrated to me by Abu Mash’ar from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
Alhamdulillaahi rabbil a’alameen four times every morning has without any doubt thanked for this day and one who says it in the night has thanked for that night.
